criteria.criterion: A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows a request that only mentions words from the old keyword table (e.g. 'deploy', 'config', 'ci', 'gate') with no governance path named is accepted by check_governance_coverage; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: The new test a_request_with_only_common_words_and_no_governance_path_is_accepted passes. It runs 14 requests built from the old table's words through check_governance_coverage and check_reading_acceptance, among them "Deploy the site on every push", "Run the tests in CI", "Add a gate before merging" and "Add a config option for the deployment gate". The old GOVERNANCE_BY_KEYWORD table refused these requests, so the test would fail on the base commit.

criteria.criterion: A unit test shows a request naming a governance path (e.g. athena.toml or .github/workflows/ci.yml) whose reading leaves it uncovered is still refused, and is accepted once it is listed and named in a criterion or named in out_of_scope; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: a_request_naming_a_governance_path_is_refused_until_it_is_covered passes. It covers 9 requests that name a governance path, including "Run the tests in .github/workflows/ci.yml" and "Change the routing in athena.toml". For each one, a reading that leaves the path out is refused; a reading that lists the file without a criterion naming it is still refused; a reading that lists and names it is accepted; and a reading that puts it in out_of_scope is accepted (reading.rs lines 4431-4467). a_request_naming_a_workflow_file_needs_it_listed_and_named and a_governance_path_that_only_looks_like_a_name_is_not_named also pass.

criteria.criterion: A test with a fake reader whose first reading is refused shows the refusal text appears in the second read's brief and the second reading is accepted and recorded; a second refusal is reported as a failure. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: In run_pin_tests, a_refused_reading_is_read_again_at_once_with_the_refusal_text_and_the_second_is_recorded passes. It shows that the first brief has no refusal section and the second brief's section contains "was refused" and the refused criterion text. The second reading is accepted, reader_error is None, two reader invocations are committed, the reading's invocation_seq is the later one, and spent_usd is 0.04. a_second_refusal_is_the_failure_and_the_reader_is_not_run_a_third_time and a_reader_that_does_not_complete_is_not_read_again also pass. The full suite passes in Athena's record.

criteria.criterion: reader_brief names each reading rule in one line and the existing brief size test passes; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
criteria.evidence: the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line passes. It checks that the section has 4 lines matching READING_RULES, each 220 bytes or fewer, and that the section names each check function and is under 1200 bytes. All 13 reader_brief tests pass. No prompt file changed, and the budgets size tests (e.g. every_role_set_is_within_its_budget) are part of the full suite, which passed in Athena's record. I found no earlier size test for the reader brief itself, so the new section-size assertion is the size limit here.

criteria.criterion: GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE is unchanged and a deliverable that is a governance file with no criterion naming it is still refused.
criteria.evidence: The diff does not touch GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE or the deliverable branch of check_governance_coverage. The new test a_deliverable_that_is_a_governance_file_is_still_refused_without_a_criterion_naming_it asserts the table's exact contents. It also shows that .github/workflows/ci.yml, defaults.toml and setup.sh, listed with no criterion naming them, are refused with "no criterion names it", and that config.rs without athena.toml is refused. The test passes.

criteria.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's records for this tree show fmt passed, clippy -D warnings passed, and cargo test passed with 1517 tests.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the narrowed governance rule and the one-time re-read with the refusal text.
criteria.evidence: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry under Fixed. It names the root cause (the word table, and the reader never being told why), describes GOVERNANCE_BY_NAMED_PATH and the paths it covers, says GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE is unchanged, and describes the single re-read in read_for with the refusal text, the recording of both invocations and the "Reading rules" section. I checked these claims against the diff and they match.

findings.summary: A changed file is outside the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: git diff HEAD~1 --stat shows run_pin_tests.rs changed (+133 lines), and it is not on the expected deliverables list. It holds the three retry tests that criterion 3 needs, which is likely why the producer put them there instead of in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, which is on the list.

findings.summary: The drain/plan read reservation does not account for the extra read.
findings.evidence: A read can now make two reader invocations, so it can cost up to twice budget.reader_usd. drain.rs is unchanged: `plan` sets aside only caps.read (`let reserve = d.caps.read;`) before each read, so a retried read could go over the `athena plan --budget` limit by up to one reader cap. The drain path sets aside caps.read + caps.run and checks again for room before the run (lines 719-760), which covers the extra read when the run cap is at least the read cap. The job's own budget is still enforced, because read_once calls check_budget before the second invocation.

findings.summary: Bare "rust-toolchain" no longer counts as naming rust-toolchain.toml.
findings.evidence: The old table used the phrase "rust-toolchain". The new phrase is "rust-toolchain.toml", and the test lists "Pin the version in rust-toolchain" as a common-word request that is accepted. A legacy `rust-toolchain` file (no extension) is a real file name, but the repository's governance path is the .toml one, so this matches the reading's assumption.

summary: The change does what the request asks. In reading.rs, the old keyword table is replaced by GOVERNANCE_BY_NAMED_PATH, so a common word such as deploy, config, CI or gate no longer requires a governance path. A path is now required only when the request names it: athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh, rust-toolchain.toml, or .github/workflows and the files under it. GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE and the rule that a listed governance file must be named in a criterion are unchanged. Athena::read_for now runs the reader once more when any reading rule refuses its reading. The second brief carries the refusal text under "# Your previous reading was refused". Only a second refusal fails, and a reader that does not complete is not run again. Both invocations are recorded and counted in the job's spend. The reader brief lists the four reading rules, one line each. I ran the targeted tests and they pass: governance (8 tests), refusal and retry (53, including the 3 new pin tests) and the reader brief (13). Athena's recorded fmt, clippy -D warnings and full test runs pass. I found two minor issues. First, run_pin_tests.rs is changed but is not on the expected deliverables list; it holds the retry tests that criterion 3 needs. Second, drain.rs is unchanged, so `athena plan --budget` still sets aside only one reader cap per read, and a read that is retried could go over that budget by up to one reader cap. The job's own budget is still checked before the second read.
